epsilon>0; delta=min(1,epsilon/5)>0. 0<abs(x-2)<delta implies1<x<3, abs(x+2)<5, abs(x²-4)<5abs(x-2)<5delta≤epsilon. All strictness conditions hold.

For fixed delta>0, h=min(delta/2,1/2) satisfies 0<h<delta; output gap4h+h² is positive. Choose epsilon=(4h+h²)/2. At x=2+h the output error exceeds epsilon although 0<abs(x-2)<delta. Thus no single delta serves every positive epsilon.
For h≠0 difference quotient=4+h, error abs(h); delta=epsilon works. abs(x) at0 has quotient+1 right,-1 left, no two-sided finite limit.

For0<x<1, t=1/x-1>0; Bernoulli induction gives x^n≤1/(1+nt); N>1/(t epsilon) suffices. For any N≥1 choose n=N and x=(3/4)^(1/n), then x<1 and error3/4>1/2, so no uniform convergence on[0,1). math_checks.claim: Soundness, consistency and two completeness notions
math_checks.derivation: Syntactic derivability entails semantic consequence under sound rules. Semantic completeness reverses this. Complete theory decides each sentence. Empty nonlogical theory with a,P has one-point models of P(a) and notP(a), hence undecided by soundness, compatible with completeness of first-order logic. Model of forallP establishes consistency while intended integers/even interpretation falsifies it.

Comprehension for x notin x yields R inR iff not(R inR). Assuming R inR derives its negation, hence notRinR; converse then derives RinR. The contradiction targets the unrestricted schema, not all self-reference or set theories.

R_A={x in A:x notin x}. R_A inR_A implies notR_AinR_A, hence notR_AinR_A. If R_AinA, definition then gives R_AinR_A, contradiction; conclude R_A notinA. No foundation assumption required; universal set impossible.

method: Closed-book derivations were recorded before reading sources. External claims were checked for scope inflation, wrong edition/year, omitted domain restrictions, and source mismatch. No large historical proof or prover was rerun.

legacy_fact_audit_gate.reason: The literal template requires two independent primary origins for confirmed. Most historical statements are author-attributed statements supported directly by one original text. Reprints, translations and mirrors are not counted as independent origins. Source support and the unfulfilled legacy corroboration threshold are recorded separately; no original cross-model or two-origin gate PASS is claimed.
